clue.text: Woman's wear close to man's wear

parts.note: nigh is an old word for near, close to
a tie is a neckwear item typically worn by men

explanation.surface: A fashion note: a woman's outfit sitting close beside a man's clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' reads as a link between the two kinds of wear, but it supplies the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightdress is a garment worn by women for sleeping.

clue.text: New article I directed to be fixed

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
led means guided or directed

explanation.surface: Someone directed to fix a new article in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hammered in with nails has been firmly secured in place.

clue.text: Good? Rubbish? This proverbially gives no indication of value

definitions.text: This proverbially gives no indication of value

parts.note: litter is rubbish left lying about

explanation.surface: A musing on whether something good or rubbish can be judged by appearances.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'All that glitters is not gold': sparkle tells you nothing about worth.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb warns that shiny sparkle is no guarantee of real worth.

clue.text: Type of photography? Bond snatches suspicious sample

indicators.note: to snatch is to grab and hold, so the bond holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a tie is a bond or link

indicators.note: suspicious suggests something fishy, so the letters of sample are not to be trusted in their order

explanation.surface: A spy story: Bond grabs a dubious sample.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests the spy 007 snatching a sample, but it is just a synonym for a link; 'suspicious' makes MELAPS from the sample.
explanation.definitionFit: Time-lapse photography takes frames at intervals to show slow change speeded up.

clue.text: Ready to get you in?

parts.note: ready is slang for cash (ready money), here the sum paid to be admitted somewhere

explanation.surface: Someone asking if you are prepared to be let in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' looks like an adjective meaning prepared, but it is the slang noun for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Admission money paid at the door is what gets you into a venue or club.

clue.text: Girl's back to snatch sailor's special chart

indicators.note: to snatch is to seize and hold, so the girl's name wraps round the sailor
back tells us the girl's name with its possessive S is read in reverse

parts.note: Pam is a girl's name, with the possessive S
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A girl returns to steal a sailor's special chart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the girl's name with its S into SMAP; the sailor sits inside after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A chart of the night sky showing the positions of the constellations.

clue.text: Bag found in odd bits of search

indicators.note: odd bits are the first, third and fifth letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A bag turns up in odd corners during a search.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology a sac is a pouch or bag-like structure in an organism.

clue.text: One tucks into a drink once more

indicators.note: tucks into means one piece is pushed inside another

parts.note: gin is an alcoholic drink
a means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: Someone tucks into a drink for the second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucks into' suggests eating; here it puts A (one) inside GIN after the opening A.
explanation.definitionFit: Again is a synonym meaning one more time.

clue.text: Musical note — what's encountered in concert?

definitions.meaning: the C nearest the centre of a piano keyboard
the letter sitting at the very centre of the word concert is C

explanation.surface: A musical note you might expect to hear at a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is cryptic: the central letter of 'concert' is C.
explanation.definitionFit: The note at the centre of the piano keyboard is called by that name; it is also the letter at the centre of 'concert'.

clue.text: Chap in butler's area being very correct?

indicators.note: in places the chap inside the butler's room

parts.note: the pantry is the room where a butler keeps provisions and silver
Ed is a man's name, a chap

explanation.surface: A man in the butler's quarters behaves with great propriety.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedantry is excessive concern with precise rules and exactness.

clue.text: What's stupid about mother using local phrases?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the stupid word goes around mother

parts.note: idiotic means stupid
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A complaint that mother is foolish for speaking in dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatic speech uses expressions natural to native speakers of a place.

clue.text: Extra soft, perhaps, but without top

indicators.note: without top tells us to lose the first letter of the word

parts.note: padded things are soft, as with a padded cushion

explanation.surface: Something extra soft, but missing its top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without top' removes the P from PADDED.
explanation.definitionFit: Added means additional, put on as extra.

clue.text: Salute former lover who's mostly spilled the beans

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: mostly means take all but the last letter of the word

parts.note: told means revealed, spilled the beans

explanation.surface: Praising an ex who has largely blabbed secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims the final D from TOLD.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly, to hail or applaud.

clue.text: Booster substance? Article about Ireland's abuse

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the article goes round the other letters

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: abuse suggests mistreatment, so the letters of Ireland are knocked out of shape

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A news article about Ireland's misuse of a stimulant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abuse' rearranges the country's letters into DRENALI, and 'about' wraps the article round them.
explanation.definitionFit: The hormone gives a surge of energy, so it is a natural stimulant.

clue.text: Chiller unusually fine and great, right? Right

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right, used again

indicators.note: unusually means in an odd arrangement, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right, used again

explanation.surface: Asking whether an unusually fine, great cooler is right, and confirming it.
explanation.definitionFit: A refrigerant is a substance used to cool things in a fridge or air conditioner.

clue.text: Apparent source of heat in June and July?

definitions.text: Apparent source of heat in June and July?

parts.words: Apparent source of heat in June and July?
parts.note: the sun appears overhead at the northern line of latitude at midsummer, while the Crab sign covers late June to late July

explanation.surface: A question about where summer heat comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: Cancer is the zodiac sign of roughly 21 June to 22 July; at the June solstice the sun is directly overhead at that line.
explanation.definitionFit: The line of latitude about 23.4 degrees north is where the sun stands overhead at the northern midsummer.

clue.text: Are Court accepting a note from planner?

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the note goes inside the other letters

parts.note: taken as the word are
a chit is a short note

explanation.surface: A court accepting a note from someone who drew up plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Are' looks like a verb but is simply its own letters; the note sits between its R and E.
explanation.definitionFit: An architect designs buildings, drawing up the plans for them.

clue.text: Baronet brings in cunning graph

indicators.note: brings in means takes inside, so the cunning word goes within the title

parts.note: Bart is the abbreviation for baronet
arch means knowing or cunning

explanation.surface: A titled gentleman introduces a crafty graph.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagram showing quantities as rectangular columns is a kind of chart.

clue.text: Fruity note apparently a source of contention

definitions.text: Fruity note apparently a source of contention

parts.words: Fruity note apparently a source of contention
parts.note: read literally it is a fruit plus a jarring musical note; idiomatically it is the golden prize in Greek myth that set goddesses quarrelling

explanation.surface: A fruity musical note seems to cause arguments.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Eris threw a golden apple marked 'for the fairest', starting the quarrel that led to the Trojan War.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means something that causes strife, from the golden prize Eris threw among the goddesses.

clue.text: Walked around third of office, looking solemn

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the walking word goes round the selected letters

parts.note: paced means walked steadily

indicators.note: a third of a six-letter word is its opening two letters

explanation.surface: Someone pacing round a third of the office with a long face.
explanation.walkthrough: A third of a six-letter word is its first two letters; 'around' wraps the walking word round them after its P.
explanation.definitionFit: Po-faced means wearing a humourless, disapproving expression.

clue.text: Capital arranged? Say more

parts.note: ran means organised or arranged, as in ran a meeting
go on is an invitation to say more

explanation.surface: Someone asking whether a capital has been sorted and urging more talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' looks like an anagram signal, but it means RAN. RANGOON is the former capital of Myanmar (Burma), now called Yangon.
explanation.definitionFit: It was the capital city of Burma until 2005.

clue.text: South Carolina border seen on a plan

parts.note: SC is the postal abbreviation for South Carolina
a hem is the border of a garment

explanation.surface: A South Carolina boundary marked on a map.
explanation.definitionFit: A schema is an outline or diagrammatic plan.

clue.text: Fierce tea brewing? Not here!

indicators.note: brewing means being made up, so the letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: Strong tea is being made, but not in this pot.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue describes a coffee press: it is for coffee, so tea is not brewed here.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafetière is a plunger pot used to make coffee, not tea.

clue.text: Big chap cheers, being in the money

indicators.note: being in tells us the thanks word sits inside the money word

parts.note: tin is slang for money
ta is informal British for thanks, as is cheers

explanation.surface: A giant of a man says thanks because he is rich.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Titans were giants, so the word means a person of great size or power.

clue.text: One almost kept back, being charged…

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: almost means drop the final letter of the phrase

parts.note: on ice means kept in reserve, held back

explanation.surface: A single person nearly held back while being accused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims the final E from ON ICE. 'Charged' suggests a crime but means electrically charged.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionic describes particles carrying an electric charge.

clue.text: … when going to bed in Berkshire

definitions.note: the definition names a place found in the county

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: Going to bed in a southern English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Berkshire is a county west of London; ASCOT, famous for its racecourse, is a town in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The racecourse town lies in that county west of London.

clue.text: Runs into mean investigator in college

indicators.note: into means the runs go inside the next word

parts.note: base means low or mean
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
a nose is slang for a detective or investigator

explanation.surface: Someone runs into a nasty detective at university.
explanation.walkthrough: Brasenose is a college of Oxford University.
explanation.definitionFit: Brasenose is one of the colleges that make up Oxford University.

clue.text: End knocked off President's vehicle

indicators.note: end knocked off means remove the last letter

parts.note: Bush is the name of two US presidents

explanation.surface: A president's car has had its end smashed.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus is a large road vehicle for passengers.

clue.text: News: it recalled the sound of bells

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word it is read backwards

parts.note: dings are ringing sounds made by bells

explanation.surface: News reminded someone of bells ringing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' suggests memory but turns IT into TI.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidings is an old word for information or news.

clue.text: Famous liner almost given a queen's name

indicators.note: almost means drop the last letter of the ship's name

parts.note: the Titanic was the famous liner that sank in 1912

explanation.surface: A famous ocean liner is nearly named after a queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Titania is queen of the fairies in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairy queen in Shakespeare's Dream bears this name.
